chapters.summary: Staff welcomes attendees to the Committee on Education vote, announces no one may approach the dais, asks devices be silenced, and invites the chair to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff opens Education Committee vote and sets dais rules

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good afternoon and welcome to today's New York City Council vote for Committee on Education.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, during today's vote, no one may approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please silence any electronic devices you may have.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz identifies himself as chair, welcomes colleagues present including Zhuang, De La Rosa, Schulman, Brewer, Louis, Narcisse, Wong, Krishnan, and notes Council Member Lee is on Zoom.
chapters.title: Chair Dinowitz opens vote and notes member attendance

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Eric Dinowitz, Chair of the Committee on Education.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Welcome and thank you to my colleagues who are present, Councilmember Zhuang, De La Rosa, Shulman, Brewer, Lewis, Narcisse, Wong, and Krishnan.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Today the committee is, and on Zoom we have Councilmember Lee.

chapters.summary: Chair states committee is voting on proposed Introduction 684-A, sponsored by Council Member Zhuang, requiring a study on how language access needs and geographic location affect access to early elementary gifted and talented programs.
chapters.title: Dinowitz announces vote on Intro 684-A for G&T language access study

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Today, the committee is voting on proposed introduction number 684A, sponsored by Councilmember Wang, a local law in relation to requiring a study on how language access needs and geographic location

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: affect access to early elementary gifted and talented programs.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz says families must know programs exist, understand consideration, and navigate deadlines often in a second or third language; access should not depend on home language or neighborhood, but city cannot currently say whether it does.
chapters.title: Dinowitz frames language and geography barriers to gifted programs

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Before enrolling a child in kindergarten, families must know that early elementary gifted and talented programs exist, understand how a child may be considered, and navigate application deadlines, often in a second or third language.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Whether a family gets through those steps should not depend on the language spoken at home or the neighborhoods they live in.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yet today, the city cannot tell us whether it does.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This bill seeks to change that.

chapters.summary: Bill requires Mayor's Office of Child Care and Early Childhood Education, with DOE and community-based early childhood providers, to study how language access and geography affect eligibility, nomination, and enrollment in K-3 gifted and talented programs.
chapters.title: Dinowitz details mandated study by child care office, DOE, and providers

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It requires the Mayor's Office of Child Care and Early Childhood Education, working with the Department of Education and community-based early childhood providers, to study how language access needs and geography affect eligibility,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: nomination, and enrollment in early elementary gifted and talented programs for kindergarten through third grade.

chapters.summary: Chair lists study components: barriers for limited English proficiency families, review of translation/interpretation/outreach, disparities by language group, borough, community district, and school district, and recommendations for multilingual households and underserved areas.
chapters.title: Dinowitz outlines four components of the G&T access study

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: An evaluation of the barriers families with limited English proficiency face at each step for first hearing about these programs to enrollment.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: A review of the translation, interpretation, and outreach the city currently conducts.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: A breakdown of disparities by language group, borough, community district, and community school district.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And recommendations aimed at multilingual households and underserved areas.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz says findings must be publicly posted within a year; recognizes diverse learning needs; says every family deserves equal opportunity regardless of zip code or English proficiency; he is a co-sponsor and supports the bill.
chapters.title: Dinowitz calls for public posting and equal access, supports Intro 684-A

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: If passed, the findings must be publicly posted within a year.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Recognizing and supporting the diverse learning needs of our children is critical to ensuring a thriving and successful school system.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Others may disagree about the importance of future of these programs, but every family deserves an equal opportunity to understand and navigate the current process.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Access to an existing public school program should not depend on family zip code or how well a parent speaks English.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This bill will give the city the information it needs to make that happen, and I'm proud to support it as a co-sponsor.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz turns to sponsor Zhuang; she thanks chair, asks colleagues to support children and families, describes barriers for immigrant, low-income, and minority families, and says bill will clarify language and location gaps.
chapters.title: Chair turns to Council Member Zhuang, who urges support for Intro 684-A

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Turn it to Councilmember Zhuang for comments about her bill.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, and thank you to be the co-sponsor of the bill, Intro 684.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Today, I'm asking our colleagues to support our children and families across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Intro 684 takes an important step toward making sure every child has a fair opportunity to access gifted and talented education programs.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: As a mom with kids in our city's public schools, I know how important it is for families to have access to those opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: But too many families, like immigrant families, low-income and minority families, face barriers that can make these opportunities feel out of reach.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: So Intro 684 helps us better understand those gaps, like how language access, location affects who learn about those programs and who get in them.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Passing Intro 684 is critical today for access and equality for all.

chapters.summary: Zhuang says a press conference will be held tomorrow in front of the Department of Education to advocate for increased educational access; every child deserves a fair shot; she thanks colleagues.
chapters.title: Zhuang announces DOE press conference and closes sponsor remarks

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And better yet, tomorrow we are holding a press conference in front of the Department of Education to continue advocating for increased

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: educational access for children because every child in New York City deserves a fair shot at great education.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz thanks Zhuang and committee staff, naming Alejandro Carvajal, Chloe Rivera, Katie Salina, Andrew Lane Lawless, and Grace Amato.
chapters.title: Dinowitz thanks sponsor and Education Committee staff

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And thank you to my staff and the Education Committee staff, Senior Councilor Alejandro Carvajal, Senior Policy Analyst Chloe Rivera,

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Policy Analyst Katie Salina, as well as Principal Financial Analyst Andrew Lane Lawless and Senior Financial Analyst Grace Amato.

chapters.summary: Chair Dinowitz turns to Committee Clerk Ben Jacobs, who calls the roll on Intro 684-A. Members vote, including Dinowitz yes, Louis aye, Brewer aye, Krishnan aye, Lee aye, Narcisse aye, Schulman aye, Zhuang aye, and Wong aye.
chapters.title: Chair directs clerk to call roll; initial roll on Intro 684-A

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I will now turn to the clerk to call the roll.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ben Jacobs, Committee Clerk, Committee on Education.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This is the roll call vote for Intro 684A.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'm a supporter of G&T, even though that might be a minority view, but I am very supportive, so I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: I for the I and as a parent going to the system.

utterances.speaker: Mercedes Narcisse
utterances.text: So, Zong, colleagues, you did a good job on that because I know I had four kids that had to go to the system.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I vote aye and congratulations to Council Member Schwing.

chapters.summary: Phil Wong announces the initial tally: 10 in the affirmative, none in the negative, and no abstentions. The vote remains open.
chapters.title: Initial tally: 10 affirmative, none negative on Intro 684-A

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: The vote stands at 10 in the affirmative, none in the negative, and with no abstentions.

chapters.summary: Krishnan says the vote will be held open; Dinowitz congratulates the sponsor. Council Member Lee asks whether her attendance was recorded, and Dinowitz confirms she is still present.
chapters.title: Committee holds vote open and confirms Council Member Lee's attendance

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Sorry, chair, did you get me for attendance?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Yeah, I mentioned you, but I'll mention you again.

chapters.summary: After a pause, the clerk continues the roll call for Intro 684-A. Council Member Gutierrez is recorded aye, and the vote is still held open.
chapters.title: Roll call resumes; Gutierrez votes aye on Intro 684-A

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Continuing the roll call vote for interest 684A, Councilmember Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And we're holding the vote open still.

chapters.summary: The clerk continues the roll call for Council Member Joseph. An aye is recorded, and staff thanks the member.
chapters.title: Roll call resumes for Joseph on Intro 684-A

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Continuing the roll call vote for intro 684A, Councilmember Joseph.

chapters.summary: The clerk announces the vote stands at 12 in the affirmative, none in the negative, and no abstentions. Intro 684-A is adopted.
chapters.title: Intro 684-A adopted 12-0

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: 12 in the affirmative, none in the negative, and no abstentions.

chapters.summary: Dinowitz recognizes Council Member Farías for attendance. She asks whether the roll call applies to the committee; Dinowitz says there is no longer quorum, thanks members, and adjourns the hearing.
chapters.title: Chair recognizes Farías, notes no quorum, and adjourns hearing

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I would like to recognize Councilmember Frias for attendance.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Is this roll call vote for our committee as well?

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: There's no longer, unfortunately, there's no longer quorum.

summary: Committee on Education held a vote on Intro 684-A, a local law requiring a study on how language access and geography affect access to early elementary gifted and talented programs.
Chair Eric Dinowitz and sponsor Susan Zhuang spoke in support, citing barriers for immigrant, low-income, and minority families; Zhuang announced a DOE press conference.
The committee called the roll, held the vote open for late members, and adopted Intro 684-A 12-0 before adjourning after noting quorum was lost.
title: Committee on Education
topic: Study on how language access needs and geographic location affect access to early elementary gifted and talented programs
